label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common), in the middle-late episode window (trials ~45-89)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 by the common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, or after any rare transition. It is also gated by time in the episode: it is silent for trials 0-39, ramps up around trial 40-49, is strongest at trials 50-89 and stops by trial 90. So it is a conjunction of the D2 a2->S2 common input with an episode clock. The predicate uses only variables observed at D2 (action and state are inputs there). All four activation quartiles are covered (dev P 0.82, R 0.98, mass recall 0.997). The remaining false positives are mostly windows where the model policy is not strongly favoring a2, or where S1 is the hidden good state: adding choice < -1.5 raises dev F1 only to 0.91, so I kept the simpler predicate. Magnitude: higher when the agent has been repeatedly choosing a2 with a strongly a2-leaning policy (rate is highest in the most negative choice-logit bins), and higher when good = S2. It is lower after a recent switch or after unrewarded and rare trials earlier in the window.

issues: The factual claims hold up. All activation mass is at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps). (D2 & a1 & S2), i.e. rare after a1, gives P 0.0001. The a1 rows show only 6 active steps out of 175k. The feature never fires after a2 -> S1 rare, since in_state = 2 is required. On the episode clock, a2 -> S2 at ep_trial < 40 and ep_trial >= 90 has P about 0. Trials 40-44 give P 0.14 and mass 0.3%, and the profile shows the ramp from 40-49 into 50-89.
Dev scores reproduce: P 0.817, R 0.980, F1 0.891, mass recall 0.997, and all four quartiles are covered at 0.92 or above.

One false-positive class the explanation does not name: the first a2 trial after an a1 trial (stay == 0, prev_action == 1). Here the predicate has precision of only 0.20 (dev 3918 predicted, test 4849). That is about 30% of all false positives. Excluding it, (stay != 0), raises test F1 from 0.882 to 0.900.
The window edges are soft. Precision is about 0.59 at trials 45-49 and about 0.53 at 85-89, against about 0.9 in the middle. The 45/90 cutoffs approximate a ramp, not a hard gate.

When good = S1, precision is 0.52 (9.9k predicted, 6% of mass). Together with choice >= -1.5 (P 0.29), this backs the stated link to the agent's lean toward a2. Adding choice < -1.5 gives test F1 0.908. This only refines the predicate and is not a counterexample to the label.
No future variables are involved: action, state and the transition are all observed at D2. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
